requirement: When an index exists, each requirement definition badge MUST link to its evidence detail page. Each detail page MUST link back to the definition's anchored badge and to the index. Reference badges MUST continue to link to the definition. These links MUST resolve when a requirement name contains `.md`, as in `requirements.cli.mdbook`.
rationale:
The code implements each clause of the requirement, and the tests cover each clause. I did not run the tests or a real mdBook build.

**Implementation**
- **Definition badge to detail page:** `replace_definitions` in `src/lib.rs` looks up `plan.detail_path(&full_name)`. If a detail page exists, it renders the badge as `<a ... id="habeas-req-NAME" href=DETAIL>`. Otherwise it renders a `<span>`. The badge keeps the anchor id that `DefinitionKind::anchor` produces.
- **Detail page back-links:** `render_detail_page` in `src/index.rs` (around lines 416–436) builds `[Requirements index](index_href) · [View definition](definition_href)`. The definition link carries the anchor `habeas-req-NAME`, so it points at the definition's badge.
- **Detail pages are generated and attached:** `IndexPlan::populate` creates each detail page and adds it as a sub-chapter of the index chapter. `is_detail_path` stops detail pages from being re-processed as definition pages.
- **Reference badges still link to the definition:** `replace_references` uses `chapter_href(current_path, &target.path, Some(anchor))`, so reference badges go to the definition anchor.
- **Names containing `.md`:** `chapter_href` is the single link builder for all of these links. It computes a relative HTML href and then replaces `.md` with `%2Emd`, which applies to both the path and the anchor.

**Tests**
- **Main index test:** `index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters` in `src/index.rs` asserts several things.
  - The definition badge has `id="habeas-req-requirements.core.ready"` and an href to `../appendix/requirements-index/requirements.core.ready.html`.
  - Index rows link to the detail pages.
  - The detail page contains `[View definition](../../requirements/core.html#habeas-req-requirements.core.ready)`.
  - The detail page contains `[Requirements index](../requirements-index.html)`.
- **Example case:** A second index test around lines 1241–1270 checks the same definition-to-detail links and back-links for an example definition.
- **Reference badges:** A test in `src/lib.rs` around line 806 asserts that reference badges for impl, cite and test link to `../requirements.html#habeas-req-requirements.ready`.
- **`.md` names:** `links_preserve_requirement_names_containing_md` in `src/lib.rs` checks `requirements.cli.mdbook`. The detail link becomes `requirements-index/requirements.cli%2Emdbook.html`. The back-link becomes `../requirements.html#habeas-req-requirements.cli%2Emdbook`. This covers both directions, including the anchor.

**Gaps**
- The `.md` case is tested at the `chapter_href` unit level, not through a full end-to-end preprocess, and I did not run an mdBook build to confirm that `%2Emd` resolves. This is minor because all the links go through that one function.
- No FIXME comments are involved.
